summary: Configured node1, node2, and node3 as a persistent three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. Multi-primary replication, one-member availability, automatic catch-up, and sequential reboot persistence all passed. Final state: all members active, Primary, Synced, Ready, and holding the identical nine-row dataset checksum.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB 10.1.48, Galera 3, and rsync on all nodes.
Configured node-specific addresses, ROW binlogging, InnoDB, rsync state transfer, causal reads, and boot-time startup.
Generated separate random TCP probe credentials locally on each node and stored them root-only.
Verified writes through every member and read/write availability with node3 unavailable.
Verified node3 automatically rejoined with writes made during its absence.
Rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time; each recovered fully before proceeding.

evidence.summary: All three services are enabled and active, directly reachable on their managed-node IPs, and report cluster size 3, Primary, Connected, Synced, and Ready.

evidence.requirement: Writes through every member replicate to the others
evidence.summary: Unique TCP writes through node1, node2, and node3 produced the same ordered dataset on every member.

evidence.requirement: Readable and writable while one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: With node3 inactive and its listeners absent, node1 and node2 remained a size-2 Primary/Synced read-write component and replicated new writes 201 and 202.

evidence.requirement: Returned member automatically rejoins with missed data
evidence.summary: An ordinary node3 service start rejoined it as Synced/Ready at size 3 with both outage-period writes; node3 then accepted a new write.
Healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgement were captured. Boot ID changed, all prior data remained, cluster size returned to 3, and rebooted node1 accepted write 301.
Healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgement were captured. Boot ID changed, all prior data remained, cluster size returned to 3, and rebooted node2 accepted write 302.
Healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgement were captured. Boot ID changed, all prior data remained, cluster size returned to 3, and rebooted node3 accepted write 303.

evidence.requirement: Final converged state after all restarts
evidence.summary: Every node reports its changed boot identity, active/enabled MariaDB, identical three-member membership, InnoDB table with nine rows, and checksum 88f862502d9c5dcb3d023ef61bb06a7c.
